bibliography.title: On the Generalization Capacities of MLLMs for Spatial Intelligence

sections.title: 5.2 Evaluation on General Spatial Reasoning Benchmarks
A Detailed Proof of Geometric Ambiguity

layout.floating_objects: Figure 1, Figure 6, Tables 2-3 span columns; other figures/tables occupy a column or top float.
layout.reading_effect: Floats carry the central visual and numerical evidence and require cross-reference to adjacent prose.

abstract_sentences.text: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) that directly process RGB inputs for tasks like 3D localization and navigation have shown remarkable potential.
However, we argue that these “RGB-only” approaches are fundamentally flawed in their ability to generalize across cameras.
By ignoring camera parameters, they entangle an object’s physical properties with the camera’s perspective, creating an irresolvable ambiguity.

evidence.anchor: entangle physical properties with camera perspective

abstract_sentences.text: We show this leads MLLMs to overfit to the training camera distribution, rather than learning true and generalizable 3D geometric principles.

evidence.anchor: overfit to the training camera distribution

abstract_sentences.text: To address this, we propose Camera-Aware MLLM framework for spatial MLLMs.

It learns generalizable spatial reasoning by: (i) injecting camera intrinsics via a dense embedding that conditions each visual token; (ii) introducing a camera-aware data augmentation strategy that synthetically varies camera parameters, forcing the model to disentangle camera properties from scene content; and (iii) distilling geometric priors from a 3D vision foundation model.

evidence.anchor: injecting camera intrinsics via a dense embedding

abstract_sentences.text: Extensive experiments demonstrate that camera-aware MLLMs substantially outperform their naive counterparts, particularly in cross-camera generalization tests on spatially-grounded tasks, indicating that camera-awareness is not only beneficial but also a prerequisite for robust and generalizable spatial intelligence in MLLMs.

introduction_moves.move: context: positions MLLMs as spatial-intelligence systems and contrasts explicit 3D representations with the scalable RGB/video paradigm.

evidence.anchor: feeding RGB images or videos directly into MLLMs

introduction_moves.move: problem → missing_insight: identifies omitted camera intrinsics, derives projected-height equivalence, and connects the ambiguity to cross-camera shortcuts.
core_idea → method_preview → result_preview: previews dense camera embedding, camera-aware augmentation, geometric-prior distillation, and cross-camera evaluation.
contribution_list: restates theoretical/empirical diagnosis, the Camera-Aware MLLM framework, and extensive verification as three contributions.

related_work_moves.move: positioning_only/taxonomy: groups general MLLM work by visual modality, alignment, and task capability without a component-level contrast.

evidence.anchor: MLLMs extend the powerful reasoning and language capabilities

related_work_moves.move: credit_or_foundation → nearest_neighbor_contrast: contrasts point-cloud/3D routes, RGB-only spatial MLLMs, and VLA models, then locates this work within RGB-only.

evidence.anchor: our work operates within this RGB-only paradigm

related_work_moves.move: limitation_of_prior → gap_creation: uses MMDE’s cross-camera failures and intrinsics-aware successes to motivate transfer of camera-awareness to MLLM spatial reasoning.

evidence.anchor: camera-awareness is a prerequisite for robust generalization

method_moves.move: state_problem: frames unknown intrinsics as the information deficit behind camera-specific shortcuts.
contrast_alternative: rejects Metric3D-style canonicalization for MLLMs because of invalid visual tokens and scarce precise K.
define_component: introduces Geometry-Aware Visual Encoder and the multimodal path from text/frames to the LLM.
define_component → derive: maps each visual-token grid coordinate through camera intrinsics to normalized ray components.
explain_mechanism: adds sinusoidal camera embeddings and fuses them with visual features by element-wise addition.

evidence.anchor: fused with the visual features via element-wise addition

method_moves.move: define_component → connect_to_prediction: varies scale and principal point while synchronizing image and K to force disentanglement.

evidence.anchor: both the image and its intrinsics are updated consistently

method_moves.move: define_component: distills a dense 3D point cloud from frozen UniDepth v2 into a geometric-prior embedding.
connect_to_experiment: uses UniDepth’s image-based intrinsic estimation to cover inputs with unknown camera parameters.
summarize: presents camera-awareness as the bridge from pixel processing to transferable geometry.

evidence.anchor: enriching them with explicit 3D structural information

experimental_design.name: task_definition
experimental_design.description: 3.1 distinguishes qualitative relational tasks from quantitative spatially-grounded tasks; §5.1 evaluates single-frame 3D detection, video 3D detection, and video 3D visual grounding.

experimental_design.name: spatially_grounded_training_corpus
experimental_design.description: The mixed corpus contains ScanNet, ARKitScenes, Matterport3D, 3RScan, SUN RGB-D, Objectron, ScanRefer, and Scan2Cap.

experimental_design.name: general_reasoning_training_corpus
experimental_design.description: General spatial reasoning training combines the LLaVA-Hound split of LLaVA-Video-178k, SPAR, and the curated spatially-grounded collection.

experimental_design.name: baselines
experimental_design.description: Cross-camera comparisons use Qwen2.5-VL and VG-LLM as task-finetuned baselines; the text says Gemini-2.5 fails 3D localization.

experimental_design.name: cross_camera_perturbation
experimental_design.description: All models train on full mixed-source data and are evaluated on ScanNet validation with synthetically resized images to perturb intrinsics; Figure 6 spans rescale factors 0.5–1.5.

experimental_design.name: ablation_setup
experimental_design.description: Ablation uses single-frame ScanNet 3D detection on ScanNet-val x1.2, created by rescaling and centrally cropping images; Table 5 reports 20 common classes.

final_judgment.single_storyline: Unknown camera intrinsics make monocular spatial MLLM observations geometrically non-identifiable, encouraging camera-specific shortcuts; token-level rays, K-consistent augmentation, and UniDepth geometric priors are the proposed repair, tested by resize curves and component ablation.〔p. 1, §1, “omission of camera intrinsic parameters”〕〔p. 6–9, §4–5〕
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The main text keeps the h_proj/equivalence setup, baseline failures, camera-intrinsics distributions, GAVE diagrams, cross-camera curves, benchmark tables, and the component ablation, preserving the decision path from ambiguity to robustness.〔p. 1–9〕
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Formal K/R/t projection and ray derivations (Eq. 3–7), scope assumptions, training/freeze/hardware/data details, the Table 6 prompt, and LLM disclosure move to Appendices A–C. Mechanism reading remains possible, but reproduction depends on Appendix B and still lacks seeds/splits/loss details.〔p. 13–15〕
final_judgment.best_pattern: The strongest pattern is to make rescaling an explicit K transformation, use the same rescale factor on the Figure 6 x-axis, and pair the failure table with a full-component ablation.〔p. 5, §3.3〕〔p. 7, Figure 6〕〔p. 9, Table 5〕
final_judgment.largest_gap: The unqualified SOTA summary in §5.2 is not closed by all aggregate rows: Ours is below VG-LLM/Gemini on Table 3 Avg and below VG-LLM on Table 4 CV Avg; synthetic resize and missing uncertainty further narrow the defensible scope.〔p. 8–9, Tables 3–4／§5.2〕
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For spatial generalization, report the input transformation, its updated K/ray field, the task denominator, and performance across the transformation in one evidence object; separate known-K and unknown-K paths.〔p. 6, §4.3〕〔p. 7, Figure 6〕
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule applies to monocular projection and metric depth/size identifiability under the stated camera assumptions; it does not by itself establish physical multi-camera deployment, all-task superiority, or unconditional SOTA.〔p. 14, Appendix A〕〔p. 7–9, §5〕
